answer: The most convincing sybil defense is vested payouts: each agent's earnings sit in a forge-style escrow and unlock over many epochs, ripening like crops on a terrace. A flash-farm of fake identities catches only a zephyr of early rewards; most of each payout unlocks only after dozens of epochs, and any collusion slash burns the unvested balance instantly. So an attacker spinning up thousands of identities forfeits nearly everything - the cost per sybil approaches the full reward it hoped to steal, making value concentrate in long-lived reputable accounts instead.
